recipe_version.title: Lemon Pea Risotto
recipe_version.description: Arborio rice stirred with hot vegetable stock until creamy, finished with peas, lemon, butter, and microbial-rennet Parmesan.

ingredients.name: Arborio rice
ingredients.note: about 10.5 oz / 300 g dry. Do not rinse. Starch is required for creaminess.

ingredients.name: frozen peas
ingredients.note: about 10 oz. Do not thaw ahead; they go in at the end. Primary vegetable.

ingredients.name: vegetarian Parmesan
ingredients.note: required dairy. A block, grated by the cook. Microbial rennet so vegetarian_compatible does not depend on a swap. Not a powdered shaker cheese.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter
ingredients.note: required dairy. Divided: 1 tbsp with the shallot, 2 tbsp to mount at the end.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: with the shallot at the start

ingredients.name: dry white wine
ingredients.note: all of it to deglaze after toasting the rice. Alcohol cooks off during simmer. Do not substitute cream here.

ingredients.name: vegetable stock
ingredients.note: kept hot in a separate pot. Vegetarian path. Do not use chicken stock if keeping vegetarian_compatible true. Unsalted or low-sodium preferred; you will season at the end.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: divided: 1/4 tsp with the shallot, then about 3/4 tsp to taste at the end depending on the stock

steps.title: Heat the stock and prep
steps.body: Bring the vegetable stock to a bare simmer in a saucepan and keep it hot over low heat for the whole cook. Finely dice the shallot. Mince the garlic. Finely grate the vegetarian Parmesan. Zest and juice the lemon. Chop the parsley. Measure the Arborio rice, frozen peas, wine, butter, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Do not rinse the rice.

steps.title: Soft the shallot and toast the rice
steps.body: In a wide heavy pot or deep skillet, melt 1 tbsp of the unsalted butter with the olive oil over medium heat. Add the shallot and 1/4 tsp of the kosher salt. Cook until soft, about 3 minutes, without browning. Add the garlic and stir 30 seconds. Add the Arborio rice and stir until the edges look translucent, about 2 minutes. This toast is part of the risotto method, not a pilaf rinse.

steps.title: Deglaze with wine
steps.body: Pour in the dry white wine. Stir until it is mostly absorbed, about 2 minutes. Do not add cream, milk, or cashew cream at any point; dairy finish is butter and Parmesan only.

steps.title: Ladle in hot stock
steps.body: Add one ladle of hot vegetable stock (about 3/4 cup). Stir often until the liquid is mostly absorbed. Continue adding stock one ladle at a time, stirring often, for about 18 to 20 minutes total ladle time. The rice should be tender with a slight bite (al dente) and the pot should look creamy from the rice starch, not soupy and not dry/stuck. You may not need every last drop of the 5 cups; stop when the texture is right. kitchen_tested is false: 18 to 20 minutes is the expected agitation window.

steps.title: Finish with peas, lemon, butter, and Parmesan
steps.body: Stir in the frozen peas and cook 2 minutes until hot and bright green. Take the pot off the heat. Stir in the remaining 2 tbsp unsalted butter, the grated vegetarian Parmesan, the lemon zest, the lemon juice, the black pepper, and enough of the remaining kosher salt to taste. Fold in the parsley. The risotto should slowly spread on a plate, not stand in a stiff mound and not pour like soup. Serve immediately. No grilled chicken on top. No cream splash beyond the butter and cheese already listed.

equipment: wide heavy pot or deep skillet
recipe_version.heat: Stock held at a bare simmer. Risotto pot over medium for shallot and toast, then medium to medium-low while ladling. Finish off heat.
recipe_version.doneness: Rice al dente with creamy starch suspension. Peas hot and bright. Spreads slowly on a plate. Lemon bright, not bitter from too much pith. kitchen_tested is false.

curator_preflight.detail: All ingredients used. Butter split 1+2 tbsp. Peas and lemon at the end. Stock ladled gradually.
1 tbsp olive oil + 3 tbsp butter (1 start, 2 mount). No cream.
Creaminess is rice starch + butter + Parmesan, not a bottled Alfredo and not cashew cream.
Prep 12 + cook 28 (3 shallot + 2 toast + 2 wine + 19 ladle midpoint + 2 peas) = 40. Stock warming starts in prep/early cook and is not double-counted as a separate oven preheat.
Base 4. Stock and rice scale; pot width matters. See scaling_notes.

scaling_notes.1: About 6 tbsp (3/8 cup) Arborio, 1/2 cup peas, 1.25 cups hot stock on hand (use what the rice needs), 2 tbsp wine, 1 tbsp butter total, 1/2 oz Parmesan, small shallot spoon, 1 small garlic clove. Use a small saucepan. Same ladle method; start checking texture at about 14 minutes.
scaling_notes.2: 3/4 cup Arborio, 1 cup peas, 2.5 cups stock on hand, half the aromatics, wine, butter, cheese, lemon. Same medium heat.
scaling_notes.4: As written. 1.5 cups Arborio, ~5 cups stock on hand, 40-minute clock.

coverage_contribution: Opens risotto as a technique/format (0 live). Italian-inspired dairy main that is not pesto pasta, mushroom walnut bolognese, polenta stew, or potato-leek gratin. Peas keep the lead ingredient out of the mushroom-bolognese cluster.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with Cashew Pesto Pasta / Mushroom Walnut Bolognese / Herbed Polenta Tomato Stew: all italian-inspired, but pasta/bolognese/polenta — not stirred Arborio risotto; those nut sauces are deliberately avoided here. Compared with Potato-Leek Gratin: both dairy, but gratin is baked potato custard; this is stovetop risotto with peas and lemon. Compared with Black Bean Quesadillas / Harissa Carrots with Feta: dairy elsewhere, different formats. Not a dairy-free cashew risotto.
